result.title: FMT: Lossless Image Compression in a Fixed Number of Parallel Steps
result.summary: Learned lossless codecs make smaller files than common classical codecs, yet the images we archive and train on still use classical codecs. A main reason is time: a learned codec takes seconds to decode a photo that a classical codec opens in milliseconds, and their faster variants give up most of their gain in size. We argue that much of this time is spent waiting, not computing: the network waits for the values it conditions on, and the arithmetic decoder reads them one at a time. We introduce FMT (Fixed-step Multiscale Tree), a lossless image format whose decoding order and entropy coder are designed together so that neither wait grows with the image. FMT stores an image as a coarse-to-fine tree whose steps hold independent values: a GPU predicts each step at once and decodes it in parallel rANS lanes that carry their states from step to step, so an image of any size decodes in a fixed number of sequential steps. On this tree we build a family of bit-exact codecs, from a rule with no network to large networks, and no codec we ran on the same GPU beats any of them on both size and speed. Without a network, FMT beats NVIDIA's HTJ2K on size and speed; with a large one, it decodes Kodak photos 9 to 61X faster than learned codecs we ran on the same A100, at the same size or smaller.

AI.brief_summary: FMT 是面向无损图像压缩的图像格式与编解码器族：它把图像组织成粗到细的树，使每一步的数值相互独立并由 GPU 并行预测，再用携带跨步状态的并行 rANS 通道解码，从而让任意尺寸图像在固定数量的串行步内完成解码。
AI.relevance_reason: 「逐步数值独立＋状态跨步携带」的并行解码设计可能为 LVR 中并行生成与更新 latent 推理状态、把串行深度固定化提供可供核查的方法线索，但该文不涉及视觉推理或答案对视觉证据的使用。
